title: copier: resolve tar entry paths through in-container symlinks (#29805)
body:
<!-- Description of the change -->
### Description
Fixes [#29805](https://github.com/containers/podman/issues/29805) where extracting a tar archive into a container (e.g., via `podman cp - ctr:/` or REST API `PUT /containers/{id}/archive?path=/`) fails with `statat var/run/x: path escapes from parent` when entry paths cross absolute symlinks inside the container filesystem (such as `/var/run` -> `/run`).

### Root Cause
In Debian, Ubuntu, and Fedora container images, `/var/run` is an absolute symlink pointing to `/run`.
When an archive containing paths like `var/run/act/actions/...` is extracted at root (`/`), `copier.Put` constructed entry paths directly without resolving intermediate in-container symlinks. Under `os.Root` path containment hardening, opening paths through absolute symlinks returned `path escapes from parent`.

### Solution
Pre-resolve intermediate symlinks for each tar header path using `resolvePath` relative to `targetDirectory`, safely re-anchoring absolute symlink targets (`/var/run` -> `/run`) inside the container rootfs before directory and file creation.

Fixes #29805

### Checklist
- [x] Signed commit (`git commit -s`)
- [x] Added system test in `test/system/065-cp.bats`
- [x] Verified path resolution for archives containing `/var/run` symlink paths
